'''''Euryops pectinatus''''', the '''grey-leaved euryops''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Asteraceae, [[endemism|endemic]] to rocky, sandstone slopes in the Western Cape of South Africa (from Gifberg to the Cape Peninsula).<ref>{{cite web 
| url= http://pza.sanbi.org/euryops-pectinatus | title = Euryops pectinatus | publisher = SANBI, PlantZAfrica.com
| accessdate = 26 February 2018}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Euryops pectinatus kz1.jpg|thumb|left|Mature shrub]]
It is a vigorous [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|2|m|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide, with silvery green, hairy leaves and yellow, daisy-like [[pseudanthium|composite flowers]] {{convert|5|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:207466-1|title=Euryops pectinatus Cass. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|website=Plants of the World Online|access-date=2019-03-25}}</ref> They bloom from early summer through to autumn and into winter in areas with mild climates.

The fruits bear a single seed and are either hairless or covered in myxogenic (slime-producing) hairs, and may also be topped by a pappus of white or brown bristles.<ref name=":0" />

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''pectinatus'' means “comb-like”,<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=184533731X }}</ref> possibly referring to the deeply-divided, fernlike leaves.

==Cultivation==
''Euryops pectinatus'' is widely used as a garden plant, especially in urban areas and due to its almost perpetual flowering regime. It grows best in full sun and well-drained deep soils. It must be grown in a sheltered location, away from frost-prone areas. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Euryops pectinatus''|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/7107/Euryops-pectinatus/Details |accessdate=19 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 38 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 26 February 2018}}</ref>
